processing: Finished black tea scented with bergamot oil and blended with dried lavender flowers; the exact recipe is up to the blender.
harvest_season: Not tied to a harvest: as with other flavoured blends, it is put together year-round from bought-in tea.
appearance_dry: Dark twisted black leaf flecked with grey-blue lavender buds.
appearance_liquor: Clear reddish amber, typical of a medium black tea.
appearance_wet: Dark brown open leaf with faded lavender buds.
taste_profile: Expect bergamot citrus with a herbal, floral lift from lavender over a plain black tea base; too much lavender can read as soapy.

brewing.notes: Western-style. Start around 3 to 4 minutes, because lavender grows louder the longer it sits.

vintage_note: Not sold by year or season, as is usual for flavoured blends: tea shops sell it year-round. The aroma is the point and it fades, so buy small amounts and keep them sealed.
description:
This is Earl Grey with one extra ingredient: black tea, bergamot and dried lavender flowers. It is a blender's idea rather than a tea from a place, and many houses make their own.

The recipe changes from one blender to the next, so the name alone tells you little about the balance or the other ingredients in the tin.

Expect citrus first, then a floral, slightly herbal finish. The usual failure is lavender taking over and tasting like soap, so judge a blend by that balance. Keep the steep moderate and adjust from there.

When buying, read the ingredient list: real lavender buds and a named oil tell you more than the name on the tin. Buy small amounts, since scented blends are at their best fresh.
history: Little is documented about the origin of this blend. No creator or date is on record; it is one of the many modern variations on Earl Grey offered by tea sellers today.
